Hot, dog crap of a game. If you play this you're a weirdo.

Forces you to create a Bethesda account to play single-player, instant negative review

Never tolerate BS

A direct downgrade from Doom 2016 in nearly every way.

I was genuinely keen to finally get around to buying and playing this after finishing Doom 2016. I expected something fairly similar in terms of the menus, UI, and overall presentation. Instead, what I got was a bloated mess packed with corporate rubbish constantly trying to shove Bethesda’s branding and online nonsense in your face.

One of the most irritating parts is that the game forces you to make a Bethesda account before you can even properly start playing. Doom 2016 just threw you straight into the action without any of this corporate account nonsense getting in the way. They care more about pushing their ♥♥♥♥ down your throat than actually letting people enjoy the game.

When I launched the game for the first time the audio was completely stuffed and I had to spend about 15 minutes messing around with settings just to get sound working properly. After finally fixing that, I loaded into my save and the intro cinematic got skipped because it "wasn't a new save". I paused the game to go back to the main menu and could not find the option anywhere at all.

The whole experience felt scuffed and frustrating before I’d even properly started playing. Absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of a game. Refunded.
They force you to create a Bethesda account. It's a single-player game for goodness' sake.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features extensive jumping and platforming puzzles that interrupt the combat flow.

citations.review_text:
"Man I wish Doom 2016 leaned a little more into what made it distinctive." A finger on the monkey's paw curls.

Eternal has a weird feel for a shooter. You have dodge tools, but you don't get them immediately and projectiles rip out so fast anyway that you're better off regen tanking. You get health back by glory killing, which means your guns are kind of just a stunning tool. Your guns have poor ammo reserves, so you use your chainsaw to reload them. As in 2016, secrets are how you progress, but Eternal has a hub world and encourages you to revisit prior stages to farm for lives.

Yeah.

I don't love the 1 Up system. I don't love the way combat feels either. I really don't love the huge amount of speedy precision platforming Eternal wants you to do, or its puzzles. All together they're a very clear vision for a game, but it's not my type of game.

I *do* like the storytelling though. This is the closest I've ever gotten to caring about Doom lore, and it does a great job both building the setting and sharpening doomguy's character. I'm sure there's a tie in novel or something to explain all the retcons and timeskips and changes from 2016, but you can kinda guess at what happened, and this is a very vibes based universe anyway.

I think if you really liked glory killing from 2016, you've gonna have an extra good time in Eternal. And if you prefer classic boomershooters, you're not going to click as much with this. It's smooth and runs cleanly though, and there's a bunch of bonus features, so if you grab it on sale it's good value per dollar.

Edit: Why are half the cutscenes unskippable on level replay? Why does the narrative stuff repeat on level replay when I'm only doing it to grind lives? Also replaying is going to be super tedious---playing anything other than the first level for lives isn't really incentivized, because it takes way longer and you get about the same amount, also there's jumping puzzles in anything after the first level and I cannot stress enough…

Huge fan of doom. However I prefer the previous doom than this one because its trying so hard to get technical with all these added powerups. Most of the time, I'd be looking for a demon to use my chainsaw so I can replenish ammo. Also, I may be wrong but I find it bothersome that shotguns and automatics both use the same type of ammo. Theres so much for so little to do with. It made the slayer less badass. And lastly of course, the classic overwhelming bethesda puzzles. Honestly these wall jumps especially during the end game were very repetitive I can tell theyre just fillers. Theyre so long and boring it just kills the vibe. Too much focus on the puzzle making rather than the action. 

I got it on sale and Im glad I did. It had so much potential but poorly executed.

Combine one of the greatest game scores of all time with peak FPS gameplay and top notch graphics while still being optimized you get this beautiful and fun game. 
There is simply nothing quite like Doom, and Doom Eternal is Doom at its peak. 

There are simply two things I didn't enjoy as much: 

1. I didn't like the large amount of jump and run passages in this game. Honestly, who goes and plays DOOM for the fun parkour?! No one right? That's why the movement is so simple - it's made for a shooter, not for a jump and run game. So why is there so annoyingly much jump and run in this gam?
2. I really loved the Gore Nests in DOOM (2016) and the incredible screams with the heavy metal music when you ripped the heart out of the gore nest. As far as I know, in DOOM Eternal these gore nests are only really a thing in these special bonus challenges. Why? Why isn't it a main progression mechanic again? Coz I really loved it in DOOM (2016). 

But still, Doom Eternal is probably better than its predecessor and on its own of course also a great game in a style which can, in this way, only be found in the DOOM gaymes.

[Intro]

The sequel to the legendary doom 2016, but marred by DRM that installed a rootkit onto your system. Now with it removed, does the game hold up?

[Graphics]

Hellscape never looked better. Enemy designs have been further pushed into more grotesque biomechanical variants along with classic demons. Also, shoutout to the skybox crew, you know who you are. Also, Demonic graffitti is a hilarious thing.

[Sound]

The music is crunch, so is everything else. Weapons, dialogue, SFX, it's all meaty and nice. Absolutely nothing to complain about here.

[Gameplay]

This is where it starts taking a turn for the worse. The thing I hated the most in the previous game was the hellsdamned jumping puzzles. They're not fun in FPS games and never will be. It just feels like tedium and annoyance. In this game, it's taken up to 11 and completely ruins the flow of the game. 

It's interesting to note that these were likely an attempt at breaking up the monotony of the game, but instead, it's just a extremely boring and aggravating mechanic. Last time I played this (before learning that it had a root kit and promptly uninstalling it) I got further than now, and there's a nice upgrade system with keys you can find lying around levels. 

The lack of ammo though, completely ruins the flow of combat for me. You will never love all the weapons in an FPS, you will always have favorites. This is like being told by a nanny to finish your veggies before you get dessert. So, with that said, no, I will not eat your damn eggplant. 

[Annoyances]

Yes extra topic time. This game has a launcher which does not shut down, and if you, the industrious person that you are, decide to shut it down, it will also shut down the main EXE. No, checking the box IN said launcher does not fracking make it go away. The game now crashes extremely frequently too, which is why I didn't finish it, because I've had this game crash ten times in about two hours of gameplay. I could troubleshoot t…

The game trades a lot of its weight and grit for:
tedious parkour
annoying timed events
guns that don't have weight even if they do damage

Every gun is a lock and every enemy type is a key. Use the wrong key and it does nothing. This makes fights annoying, tedious, and deadly if you don't already know what types of enemies are about to appear. 
There are also constant pop ups as you play the game spoon feeding you every enemy weakness, and new mechanic in text blocks.
 It feels like an the sequel to Doom 2016 was made by an entirely different team. A team that had an entirely different and opposing vision to the first title

Is it possible that id Software can follow up their 2016 reboot with an even more brutal, demon hating, raged filled Doom Slayer?  Turns out yes.  With even more finishers and collectables.  

The minor story (that is really just something in the background for those interested and gives just enough "why" for pushing you to the next combat chamber) is not as enjoyable as the last game but that really isn't the focus here.  You don't even need to know what is going on other than kill the demons to open the next door.

The fights in this game are intense!  You will be overwhelmed, hunting for ammo, beating some poor lower demon to death for some health.  And yet, it is tons of fun!  If you can be bothered to learn some enemies are weaker to certain weapon types or have unique mechanics to make them easier to kill.  And hell if there are a lot of different enemies in this game.  Marauders suck though.  They are just annoying and do not flow with the nonstop action game play of the rest of the game.

Any who, this game overall is bad ass and if you like running and gunning just like the 2016 doom then you'll be right at home!

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Overcoming the initial learning curve and platforming elements unlocks the core combat loop.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe a steep learning curve and report having to adapt their playstyle or overcome initial frustration before the combat loop clicks.

citations.review_text: DOOM Eternal is a fantastic FPS and a true evolution of the genre, even if I still prefer DOOM (2016). The learning curve is huge, I actually rage quit the first time because I tried playing it like DOOM (2016). But once the combat loop finally clicks, it becomes incredibly addictive and satisfying. The faster, more strategic combat is excellent, exploration is fun, and the automap system makes hunting for secrets genuinely enjoyable. I also like the more colorful, arcade like style, although I personally prefer the darker tone and atmosphere of DOOM (1993) and DOOM (2016). My biggest complaints are the excessive parkour and some of the boss fights, which can feel frustrating compared to how amazing the normal combat is. The Ancient Gods DLCs are also great, even though I had similar issues with their bosses. I still wish we could get another simpler, modern DOOM like DOOM (2016) without such a steep learning curve, but I respect what id Software accomplished with DOOM Eternal. It takes risks, pushes FPS combat forward, and creates something incredibly rewarding once you learn how to play it. My ranking: DOOM (2016) is my favorite, DOOM (1993) comes second, and DOOM Eternal takes third place. Highly recommended for every DOOM fan and anyone who loves challenging FPS games. 9/10
I have to admit, it took me a bit of a while for the game to click with me but, man ... Once it did ... It is amazing.

TLDR: DOOM Eternal is one of the most adrenaline filled shooters I've played. If you enjoy fast paced combat that constantly pushes you to think on your feet, it's an easy recommendation. If getting overwhelmed by chaos stresses you out, this might not be the game for you.

I completed the main campaign on Nightmare difficulty without ever having played DOOM (2016), and I now  genuinely understand why this series has such a dedicated fanbase. What surprised me the most wasn't just how fast the game was, but how quickly it teaches you to think under pressure. Every encounter feels like controlled chaos, forcing you to make split second decisions while constantly adapting to what's happening around you.

The combat is where DOOM Eternal truly shines. You're rarely standing still, and the game rewards aggression far more than playing it safe. Enemy variety keeps encounters interesting, and learning how to prioritize different threats becomes just as important as having good aim. Rather than relying on a single overpowered weapon, I found myself using nearly every gun in the game because they all had a purpose and were genuinely fun to use.

What I enjoyed most was the feeling of always having to think one step ahead. Every fight became a balancing act of managing your resources, positioning yourself, and deciding which enemy needed to go first. Once that gameplay loop clicks, the combat becomes incredibly satisfying and every victory feels earned.

If you're looking for a slower, more methodical shooter, this probably isn't for you. But if you enjoy games that constantly test your reflexes, decision making, and ability to stay calm during chaos, DOOM Eternal is the game for you.

Doom Eternal is amazing. 

Ngl I played this game for a bit a long time ago and ended up ragequitting because at the time I did not understand what was required of me to exist in it's world. It is not just a mindless run and gun game, no no no, Eternal requires you to be calculated in your movements, enemy priority, and weapon switching if you want to succeed. Initially the thought of dialing in the weapon switching seemed like a daunting task. I was kinda overwhelmed by the fast paced nature of the game and having to micromanage so many resource replenishment systems and remembering every key that was bound to each individual weapon, but at a certain point it clicks, and when it does this game becomes one of the best playgrounds for skill expression and brutalizing your enemies. 

100% recommend this game if you are the type of person that enjoys a challenge and extreme levels of "math in the moment" type gameplay. ♥♥♥♥♥ so good your periphery will completely shut down while playing it.

You know what, after several tries i wasn't getting past first level, and left this gem behind. 
Now i give it another try, and after some trial and error the game just clicks. It is awesome.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe a combat system featuring resource management mechanics such as using the chainsaw for ammo, flame belch for armor, and glory kills for health.

citations.review_text: Great game. People that say its too hard or frustrating just don't understand the game. When I first started, it was hard due to the fact that I was used to Doom 2016. At the start you don't get much and you can no longer punch to kill/damage for glory kill, it only staggers them. If you dodge/boost into them, it does damage, very minor of course, but it will allow glory kill after a while. The whole point of the gameplay is to use everything they give you throughout the game in order to win. You cannot just focus on healing or attacking, you have to do both. You get a chainsaw in the beginning that you MUST use in order to get ammo. The difference between 2016 and eternal with the chainsaw is that the fuel refills up to 1/3 automatically, regardless of getting a jerry can from the ground. In 2016, you would find ammo on ground more often. This is supposed to inspire the player to constantly get ammo and swap weapons. Swapping weapons is also forced upon the player for weak points on demons to bring them down quicker as well as using certain mods for weapons on certain demons. You use flame belch on large groups of enemies and use blood plunch or AoE weapons like the rocket launcher to gain lots of armor and perform glory kills for more health or combine the two. Additionally, using the super shotgun with firery meat hook to essentially flame belch one target and shoot them when close enough to gain armor and move around the map more is another must use. Moving around the map is also important for staying alive. Try out different combos of weapons in certain situations to overcome your enemies. You cannot run as fast like in doom 2016, so you gotta use your dodge/boost and jumping with meat hook on super shotgun to get around quickly to other obstacles that you can use to jump. The art style isn’t as good to me as Doom (2016), feeling a bit more stylized and less grounded compared to the gritty militaristic sci-fi tone of the previous game. The orange filter that's on the base game got remedied a bit by the "gritty" filter under the film grain settings.

9.1/10

If you liked DOOM 2016 then ETERNAL is that but 10x better. The movement is improved, the combat feels more satisfying,  the music just does not get boring to listen to even after 200 hours and the game is greatly optimized.  Honestly what more do you want you should just play it mainly because of the music.

The best arena based FPS games I've ever had the pleasure of playing through for over 6 years now. DOOM Eternal takes everything from Doom 2016, gives it a new shiny coat of AAA paint, gives us a insanely tight combat loop that requires proper mastery of all your weapons, and dials the action up to an 11. It's fast, it's addicting and there's nothing else on the market quite like this game. 

While 2016 was more of a Run-and-Gun type of game, DOOM Eternal is all about speeding around like a fighter jet killing demons in masterfully crafted arenas. The game is an absolute spectacle and there's tons of replayability
with the different modes of play, as well as The Ancient Gods campaign expansions. It truly is a love letter to Doom, and gaming as a whole. The combat loop is some of the most satisfying I've seen in any arena shooter to date. It takes some getting used to, but when you get the hang of it you feel unstoppable.


TL;DR Me go fast, guns go brrrt, music is great and the demons are dead :]

Justice for Mick!
